topics: tenant isolation and noisy neighbor mitigation
retry budget and exponential backoff config
KV cache warmup and probe traffic
meeting_header: Date: 2027-04-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Jordan Blake, Evelyn Park (Redwood); Ravi Menon, Sophie Li, Diana Ortiz (Catalyst Health)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, um, started recording. quick agenda: go over the late last week 5xx events, propose mitigation steps, and confirm next steps.
[00:18] Ravi: yeah thanks Jordan. we saw a cluster of 502s around 02:10 UTC when our daytime batch overlapped with customer traffic, so heat map looked like a hotkey surge to a subset of tenants.
[00:35] Evelyn: okay, quick clarifying question, when you say hotkey, is that a single prompt template or are you seeing a small set of user ids?
[00:45] Sophie: mostly a handful of user ids, looks like uid-23 and uid-77 plus a sudden increase in suggestions API calls that hit longer seq lengths.
[01:02] Jordan: got it. initial hunch is noisy neighbor + cold kv cache + request burst that blew past our concurrency limit and caused upstream queueing which then returned 502s.
[01:15] Diana: is that the same as the timeouts we saw earlier this month? those were more spread out.
[01:25] Evelyn: similar symptom, slightly different mechanism. timeouts were mostly per-request latency tail; these are backend 502 responses when the serving runtime rejected or failed. both can be addressed by a mix of tenant isolation, probe warmups, and smarter retry/backoff on client side.
[01:44] Ravi: walk me through tenant isolation option please, how invasive is it?
[01:50] Jordan: it's a config flag we can flip for the pilot that pins tenants to dedicated worker pools for a short window. not full-dedicated capacity but soft isolation—reduces noisy neighbor impact by restricting co-tenancy. requires a restart of a subset of workers; negligible downtime if done staged.
[02:10] Sophie: will isolation increase cost? our CFO is sensitive.
[02:14] Jordan: minimal for the pilot since it's temporary and uses existing nodes; long-term dedicated capacity affects billing. we can estimate delta and share numbers.
[02:25] Diana: what about retries? our client SDK already retries but we see amplified traffic.
[02:32] Evelyn: yes, that was a big point. the customer retry pattern is aggressive: 5 retries with linear 200ms backoff. that amplifies bursts. we propose a client retry budget: e.g., 2 tries with jittered exponential backoff starting at 100ms, max 1200ms, and a per-client circuit breaker to prevent retry storms.
[02:57] Ravi: any reference config?
[03:00] Evelyn: we'll upload a sample JSON backoff policy, but high level: max retries 2, initial backoff 100ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.2, ttl for circuit breaker 30s. also recommend using idempotency keys for inference when applicable to avoid double work.
[03:18] Sophie: idempotency for generation is tricky but for embeddings and rerank it's easy.
[03:23] Jordan: also worth mentioning KV cache warmup—if you saw long-seq requests, cold KV means model spends more time fetching state which increases latency and can result in timeouts under load. our suggestion is probabilistic warmup/probing for hot keys prior to peak windows.
[03:42] Ravi: we run daily batch jobs that align to a predictable window, could we schedule warmups then?
[03:48] Evelyn: exactly. a 10-15 minute probe across the small set of hot keys before traffic spikes reduces cold-start tail. we'll provide a script.
[03:58] Diana: telemetry—what do you need from us to validate?
[04:02] Evelyn: three things: request traces with timestamps and full headers for the error window, aggregate per-tenant QPS during the window, and the stack traces for any 502 payloads you have. those let us correlate queue saturation vs runtime errors.
[04:18] Ravi: Sophie can export but we need to scrub user data. is a secure upload accepted?
[04:22] Jordan: yes, use the secure S3 bucket we shared in the onboarding deck, or send via SFTP. we'll put the link in CRM.
[04:30] Sophie: okay we'll scrub and upload by next week.
[04:34] Jordan: next, fallback routing—if we detect sustained high error rate for the pilot model, we can route to a smaller low-cost variant that has higher availability but slightly lower quality, until the windows clears. thoughts?
[04:47] Ravi: acceptable if quality impact is minimal and we get clear circuit breaker thresholds.
[04:52] Evelyn: we propose: trigger fallback when 5xx rate > 2% for 60s and sustained CPU saturation on the node group; fallback window max 5 minutes then reevaluate. that's tunable.
[05:06] Diana: can you show us the telemetry thresholds in the dashboard?
[05:09] Jordan: yes, we'll create a short dashboard preset and share.
[05:14] Sophie: there was also a spike of 504s earlier which looked like long-running ops getting cancelled. is that related?
[05:21] Evelyn: related in the sense of upstream queueing; some requests hit request time budgets. the platform has timeouts at multiple layers—client, load balancer, runtime. we need to align them so client-side retries respect server timeouts and don't reissue when a request is already in progress.
[05:40] Ravi: ok, so what's the plan for the next 7 days?
[05:44] Jordan: immediate: enable tenant isolation flag for the pilot and run a 1-hour blast test to observe error modes. parallel: change client retry policy in staging to the proposed settings. Sophie to upload traces. then we reconvene with deeper RPC tuning.
[06:00] Diana: will Redwood run the blast test or we do it?
[06:04] Evelyn: Redwood will run the isolation blast against a copy of your traffic profile in our dedicated test harness; we prefer to use your anonymized traces. that gives apples-to-apples telemetry.
[06:15] Ravi: can we get a simple checklist to follow so our on-call knows what to toggle? last time toggling caused confusion.
[06:22] Jordan: yes, we'll package a runbook with clear toggles: enable isolation, enable warmup probes, apply retry profile, monitor thresholds, rollback steps.
[06:31] Sophie: great. about the warmup probes, any chance we can automate based on upcoming scheduled batches?
[06:37] Evelyn: we can add a cron-triggered probe or a webhook that listens to your scheduler. small engineering lift on both sides.
[06:44] Ravi: cost question again—if we do isolation for the pilot during peak windows only, any estimate?
[06:50] Jordan: rough estimate: 5-8% increased token cost during the isolation window for the pilot, but we'll produce a detailed delta after we run the 1-hour test.
[06:59] Diana: what about alerting? we want to avoid alerts flooding our SRE rotations.
[07:04] Evelyn: recommended: aggregate error alerts with a short suppression window, and have a high-severity pager only for sustained high-5xx > threshold. lower severity can be routed to a channel. we can provide sample alert rules for Prometheus/Datadog.
[07:18] Sophie: are there any configuration toggles on your side to reduce 5xx likelihood? for example, queue sizing or dropping long requests early?
[07:26] Evelyn: yes, queue sizing and early drop policies are configurable, but they trade availability for throughput. we usually prefer graceful degradation: fallback to lower-cost model or rate-limit by tenant rather than throwing hard drops.
[07:40] Ravi: okay that aligns with our risk posture. Diana: what about SLOs—do you have suggested SLOs for a pilot?
[07:48] Jordan: suggested SLO: p99 latency < 1.5s for short prompts, error rate < 0.5% overall, and an agreed rollback policy. for pilot we can be more lenient and focus on reducing tail.
[08:00] Diana: fine. let's talk timelines and cadence.
[08:03] Jordan: action items captured: Evelyn to run blast with isolation (due 4-9), Ravi/Sophie to upload traces (due 4-12), Jordan to share playbook and dashboard presets (due 4-8). reconvene 4-14 for RPC/backoff params.
[08:18] Ravi: one more thing—could the 5xx have been from a misconfigured ingress or client library? we recently upgraded our proxy.
[08:26] Evelyn: possible. please include proxy upgrade logs with the traces. sometimes connection pooling changes in proxies cause reset patterns that look like 502s.
[08:35] Sophie: will do.
[08:37] Jordan: ok last bit—we'll also enable adaptive KV cache prefetch for the pilot which selectively warms top 200 keys. that should cut tail.
[08:48] Ravi: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:51] Diana: thanks.
[08:53] Jordan: we'll follow up in CRM with links, playbook, and the runbook. meeting adjourned.
